keyVerseText: Zebulun and Naphtali were a people that jeoparded their lives unto the death in the high places of the field. jeoparded: Heb. exposed to reproach
rootMeaning: The Hebrew noun מָרוֹם (mârôwm) derives from the root רוּם (rûwm), which conveys the idea of lifting up, elevating, or exalting. This root emphasizes not only physical height but also a sense of exaltation or elevation in status. Thus, מָרוֹם carries the literal sense of something set high or lifted up, which enriches its common English glosses like "on high" or "height" by including the nuance of dignity and loftiness beyond mere spatial elevation.
usageInScripture: Throughout Scripture, מָרוֹם appears 54 times, predominantly translated as "on high" (13 occurrences), but also as "from above," "in the high places," and "of the high ones." This range of translations shows the word's consistent association with elevated physical locations as well as elevated status or authority. Its use in both concrete and figurative senses reflects the multifaceted concept of height, whether referring to geographical elevation or noble dignity.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding מָרוֹם as height or exaltation deepens our grasp of God's transcendence and majesty, as He dwells in the highest places, far above all earthly powers. This word reminds believers that God's authority and presence are supreme and lofty, inviting reverence and trust. Moreover, the notion of elevation ties into Christ's exaltation, who is seated at the right hand of the Father, embodying divine dignity and honor. Recognizing מָרוֹם's layered meaning enriches faith by highlighting God's sovereign rule from above and His call for believers to live in humility rather than pride.
keyVerseReflection: Judges 5:18 states, "Zebulun and Naphtali were a people that jeoparded their lives unto the death in the high places of the field." The use of מָרוֹם here emphasizes not only the physical elevation of the battlefield but also the noble courage and risk undertaken by these tribes. The "high places" symbolize a setting of exposure and honor, where faithfulness and valor are demonstrated. Thus, מָרוֹם contributes a sense of elevated sacrifice and steadfastness in the face of danger.
